title: Arc Welding in All Positions — Theory and Safety Awareness
objective: Recognise that arc welding work is classified by welding position and understand why position, approved procedures, quality requirements and safety controls matter, without performing welding work.

curriculum_traceability.knowledge_topic: KM-06-KT06 — Arc welding in all positions
curriculum_traceability.primary_source: QCTO occupational curriculum hosted by CHIETA — Curriculum-6.pdf

safety_boundary: Knowledge and safety-awareness only. This lesson does not teach arc-welding setup, machine settings, electrode selection, ignition, electrode movement, welding sequence, body positioning, joint preparation or how to perform a weld in any position. Practical welding belongs in authorised occupational training under competent supervision.

sections.heading: 1. Why welding position matters
sections.body: Welding positions describe how a joint is oriented when welding work is performed. Recognising the required position is part of understanding the job information and the approved welding procedure.

sections.heading: 2. Position families
sections.body: Welding work may be classified using position families such as flat, horizontal, vertical and overhead. Different standards may use different position codes, so the applicable drawing, specification and approved procedure must be consulted.

sections.heading: 3. Arc welding across positions
sections.body: The occupational curriculum requires knowledge that arc welding may be encountered across different welding positions. This lesson develops recognition of that concept only and does not teach the practical technique for any position.

sections.heading: 4. Standards and qualification
sections.body: Welding positions form part of welder training, qualification and fabrication requirements. A learner should understand that practical competence is demonstrated and assessed under authorised training and applicable standards, not established by completing a theory lesson.

sections.heading: 5. Quality requirements remain controlled
sections.body: Weld quality is judged against the applicable specification, code and inspection requirements. The welding position does not remove the need for controlled workmanship, inspection and authorised acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: 6. Safety awareness
sections.body: Arc-welding environments can involve serious hazards including electrical energy, intense light and heat, fumes, hot material and fire risk. Practical training therefore requires workplace controls, suitable protective measures and competent supervision.

sections.heading: 7. Changing position changes the task context
sections.body: A change in joint orientation can change how the welding task is classified and how an approved procedure applies. Learners should recognise the position specified for the work rather than assuming that all welding situations are equivalent.

sections.heading: 8. Stop and refer
sections.body: If the welding position, process, drawing, specification, standard or approved procedure is unclear, stop and refer the matter to a competent trainer or supervisor before practical work is attempted.
